$comment: Pre-registration of the #501 query-time cross-encoder rerank DECISION (§18.3). Registered before a single quality number exists. #501 is a decision issue: the deliverable is a table plus a recommendation to Daniel, not a shipped reranker. The prose version, with the model spike that produced the numbers below, is docs/design/2026-09-09-501-cross-encoder-rerank-messplan.md. Amending anything after a run has started invalidates that run: bump registration_version and say which version a report belongs to.
$comment_status: structure_registered — the free parameters, slices, metrics and decision bars are fixed; no quality or latency number has been produced yet. #500 (LongMemEval as the external arm) is the precondition and must have landed before the LongMemEval side runs.
question: The remaining recall deficit is mis-ranking, not missing recall (#103: hybrid keeps 99/115 far golds in the pool at R@3 far 70.4%; #118: a deeper pool pulls in 12 more of which NONE reaches the top 3). Does a cross-encoder — the one mechanism that looks at the query and a candidate together — fix the order, and does the lift pay for the latency?
not_in_scope: Wiring a cross-encoder into the production recall path. Zero production latency impact from this work.
Score blending between the cross-encoder logit and the RRF score — a second free parameter, registered separately only if the simple form carries.
Quantizing the main arm: its repo ships no quantized ONNX and a self-conversion is its own undertaking, considered only if the lift carries.

insertion_point.$comment: Where a rerank stage WOULD sit, and why measuring it needs no production change at all.
insertion_point.would_sit: between staleness.rank and slice(0, k) in SearchIndex.recallHybrid
insertion_point.measured_through: opts.onCandidatePool (#121, packages/core/src/search.ts:1226) — the damped, pre-slice pool, in the same order and on the same score scale as the served hits
insertion_point.pool_depth: HOP_SEED_POOL = max(k*4, 20); at PRODUCTION_K = 10 the pool is 40 deep, so N up to 30 is measurable without moving a shipped constant
insertion_point.ceiling: The pool is bm25Top(50) ∪ vectorTop(50). A gold outside it cannot be rescued by any reranker, so recall_any@N is reported per run — without it a small lift is indistinguishable from an exhausted lever.

free_parameters.$comment: Fixed here, before the first number. The passage length is on this list because the spike showed it moves cost by a factor of 3.4 — more than N does — which makes it a registered choice rather than an implementation detail.

passage_modes.body: title + summary + body[0..400] — measured at ~191 tokens/pair

free_parameters.fusion: pure rerank ranking; the cross-encoder logit orders the window alone, ties keep RRF order
free_parameters.staleness: applied BEFORE the rerank — the pool handed out is the damped one, which is where the stage would sit in production
free_parameters.resampling: paired per case; 10,000-iteration percentile bootstrap CI and a two-sided sign-flip permutation test, the same construction rrf-k-beir.ts used for RRF_K
free_parameters.acceptable_alternatives: The primary uses expected_ids only — which MATCHES goldset-run.ts's headline recall_at_3 (it scores rank_expected). Its rank_any companion is reported beside it as at_incl_acceptable, so the two harnesses can be laid side by side without a hidden divergence.
free_parameters.pool_size_buckets: Median of poolSize over the run's answerable cases, computed IN-RUN (assignPoolBuckets) and reported as pool_split. Fixed by construction, the same discipline longmemeval-run.ts applies to its near/far cut. Explicitly NOT a cut on the RRF score — that would be a disguised weak_result variant. DEGENERACY IS CHECKED: the pool is near-constant by construction (bm25Top 50 union vectorTop up to 50, cut to HOP_SEED_POOL = max(k*4,20) = 40), so on a vault well over 50 memories poolSize is 40 for practically every query, the median is 40, every case lands in `large` and `small` is empty. Both buckets are always emitted and a split that did not split marks by_pool not_evaluable in the artifact — otherwise `by_pool: {large: {n: 584}}` would read like a result and the above_pool_size shape would be dead behind a plausible mechanism. This is a PREDICTION derived from the code, not an observation; it is falsified if the vector arm routinely returns fewer than ~40 hits after filtering, and the warning then stays silent.

models.$comment: Spiked 2026-09-09 on an Apple M4 Pro through transformers.js (ONNX Runtime in Node). Real loads, real pairs. Ollama was ruled out because it has no rerank endpoint — a cross-encoder is a sequence classifier, not a generator.

en-de.spike: DE query: gold +1.75, related distractor -7.41, unrelated -10.97 / -11.10. Graded, not just separated.

bge.spike: DE query: gold -3.01, distractors ≈ -10.18 — works, but the negative tail is flat.
bge.why_reference_only: 956 ms p50 at N=30 is over the ~500 ms hook budget before any retrieval. It answers the one question the cheap model cannot: is the hypothesis wrong, or was the model too weak?

ms-marco.spike: EN (Berlin classic): gold +8.85, distractor -11.25 — works. DE: gold -11.16, distractor -11.30 — NO SIGNAL AT ALL.
ms-marco.$comment_guard: Running this on the German gold set would produce a number that reads as 'reranking does not help' and means 'this model does not speak the language'. rerank-model.ts carries the language list as a guard for exactly that reason.

rejected.onnx-community/bge-reranker-v2-m3-ONNX: 568M params, XLM-R-large class — certainly over budget given the bge-base numbers
rejected.onnx-community/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-ONNX: causal LM with a yes/no logit; not a SequenceClassification head, high integration cost, certainly over budget
rejected.jinaai/jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingua: XLM-R base class, cost profile coincides with bge-reranker-base

datasets.$comment: The two sets are not the same language, and the main arm is bilingual. Without a fixed assignment a cross-set model comparison would measure languages instead of models: on English LongMemEval the English-only ms-marco could beat the bilingual favourite while saying nothing about our production case.

longmemeval.role: externally comparable control figure, plus the probe of whether the bilingual arm costs quality on English

datasets.$comment_divergence: A lift that appears on LongMemEval and not on the gold set is not a contradiction — it is a language finding, and the recommendation follows the gold set.

slices.$comment: Registered now so no slice can be discovered after the fact to rescue a null result.
slices.lang_de_vs_en: The main arm is bilingual; whether it carries on both sides is a number, not an assumption.
slices.neutral_vs_prose: 205 of the 584 answerable gold cases carry lang=neutral — keyword chains out of hooks ('memory format schema json yaml frontmatter'), not questions. A cross-encoder is trained on natural-language pairs. If the lift is prose-only, 'prose queries only' is a legitimate recommendation shape, and it has to be visible in the data rather than invented afterwards.
slices.mixed_not_evaluable: lang=mixed is 4 cases. Any slice below MIN_SLICE_N=30 is reported as not_evaluable with its n instead of as an interval: a percentile bootstrap over four paired 0/1 deltas describes the resampling, not the data.

no_answer.$comment: A reranker can raise R@3 and still hurt, by confidently promoting something on a question that has no answer. The 79 no_answer cases run as a guard, never as a lift metric.
no_answer.reported: how often the top position changes under rerank
no_answer.consequence: a regression here vetoes the 'always on' recommendation regardless of R@3
no_answer.limit_of_the_metric: A top-1 change on an unanswerable question is NOT harm — there is no right answer there and both candidates are equally wrong. The metric measures only whether the rerank reorders that subset SYSTEMATICALLY. The 20% threshold is a veto trigger and must never be read as a quality statement.
no_answer.threshold: veto 'always on' when the top-1 position changes on more than 20% of the no_answer cases (>15 of 79)

guards.regression_share: rank_regression_share: share of cases whose first expected id ends at a worse rank in the served, floored list (falling out of it counts as worst). Threshold 15%. This replaces 'no gold loses rank', which is never satisfied over hundreds of cases and would therefore have excluded 'always on' independently of the data — a dead criterion, not a strict one.

latency_protocol.$comment: Ollama and the cross-encoder share this machine. A naively differenced end-to-end time would charge the reranker for whatever the dense arm was doing.
latency_protocol.measurement: an hrtime span around the rerank stage INSIDE the call — whatever a case cost in recallHybrid sits outside the span entirely
latency_protocol.baseline: the same call without the rerank, timed at the same place
latency_protocol.batches: real N-sized batches; everywhere else one deep scoring pass covers every N, but here the batch size IS the question
latency_protocol.cold: first scored batch in a fresh process, with the model file cached and the network off; model load (446-507 ms measured) is reported BESIDE the score times and never folded into a 'cold p95' — it is a prewarm-lane cost (#361), not a recall cost
latency_protocol.contention: vector.search wait_ms / timed_out / provider_outcome are logged per run; a run with a conspicuous dense-arm timeout rate is DISCARDED, not interpreted. No other model work on the machine during a latency run.
latency_protocol.hardware: Apple M4 Pro — the FAST side of the hardware tiers. Every latency figure is a LOWER BOUND and is labelled as one. No hardware matrix is built. The useful direction: what is already marginal here is decided everywhere; a comfortable figure here says nothing about an 8 GB machine, which is why #492 exists.
compared_against: cumulative context budget (#458) — not a time budget, but a rerank changes what fills it

decision_bars.$comment: Written before the first number. Estimator throughout: paired bootstrap CI95. Values in percentage points. A small lift is a fully acceptable outcome.

all_of: primary: delta < 2.0 pp OR CI95 includes 0
none of only_on_weak_result / prose_only / above_pool_size clears its own bar
bge at N=30/body on the gold set shows the same (delta < 2.0 pp or CI95 includes 0)
close_501.mandatory_classification: see effect_classification — 'no effect' and 'no affordable effect' are different findings and the report must say which

all_of: primary: CI95 lower bound > 0 AND delta >= 2.0 pp

language veto: on neither de (n=272) nor en (n=103) is the CI95 UPPER bound < 0. Stated as an upper bound, not a point estimate: en at n=103 can produce a negative point estimate from noise, and only 'this slice is demonstrably harmed' should veto
latency: added p95 <= 50 ms at N=10/short ON THE M4 PRO — deliberately strict because it is a lower bound
no_answer guard: top-1 changes on <= 20% of cases
recall_any@10 < 100% — otherwise the lever is exhausted by construction and the lift cannot be coming from the rerank

only_on_weak_result.subset: cases where isWeakResult(served baseline, true) is true — the shipped predicate from packages/core/src/weak-result.ts, wired into the harness, not reimplemented
all_of: at least 50 cases in the subset, otherwise reported 'not evaluable' rather than as a result

prose_only.slices: prose = de + en + mixed (379 cases); keyword = neutral (205)
all_of: prose: delta >= 2.0 pp AND CI95 lower bound > 0
prose_only.why: a cross-encoder is trained on natural-language pairs; the hook lanes that emit keyword chains would carry only the cost

all_of: large-pool half: delta >= 2.0 pp AND CI95 lower bound > 0

unresolved_fallback.$comment: B5. Not a precedence problem — precedence orders OVERLAPPING rules, and this is the case where NONE matches. The review constructed it: +3.0 pp at N=30 with CI [+1.2, +4.8], only +0.6 pp at N=10, even across languages, no pool concentration, p95 286 ms. It is not an exotic corner: the 50 ms bar is already broken by short/N=20 at 52 ms, so an affordable-only-at-depth result is a likely outcome.
unresolved_fallback.rule: When no shape above matches, the recommendation is DO NOT SHIP, plus the mandatory effect_classification, plus the exact reason no shape matched. The default is never 'ship the best-looking arm'.

big_lift_unaffordable_latency.$comment: The special case named in version 1 but left undefined. 'Large' now has a number.
big_lift_unaffordable_latency.definition: some arm reaches delta >= 5.0 pp at R@3 with CI95 lower bound > 0 while its added p95 exceeds the 50 ms bar
big_lift_unaffordable_latency.consequence: not 'on' and not merely 'close'. It means query-candidate interaction carries and only the query path cannot pay for it — positive evidence for #119 (cross-encoder offline over doc2query expansions at write time), and it must be written into the recommendation as such.

non_measurement_factors.$comment: These belong in the recommendation to Daniel and are not answered by any number here.
non_measurement_factors.language_island: The main arm is EN+DE. For a user with a Russian or Spanish vault it would be exactly what ms-marco is for us — a model with no signal (#480 names those users). 'Always on' would therefore be a German island solution unless a genuinely multilingual model fits the budget, and bge-reranker-base fits linguistically but not temporally.
non_measurement_factors.hardware: See latency_protocol.hardware. The same stage costs a multiple on the 8 GB baseline and nobody has measured it there.

dependency.$comment_version: 4.2.0 is the version the spike numbers above were measured on.
constraints: must appear in no runtime dependency of core or daemon
is REMOVED again if #501 ends in 'close it'

footprint.$comment: Counted against the lockfile state before the install, not estimated. Reported because it is not a small appendix.
footprint.$comment_sharp: sharp is an image library transformers.js brings along for image models we never touch. Carried, not needed. If this ever became a production dependency, that is the point at which a leaner ONNX binding would have to be found.

dependency.$comment_hono_correction: Commit f095a94's message claims the lock refresh pulled @hono/node-server from 2.0.5 to 2.1.1. It did not: 2.1.1 was already in the lockfile at 3476718 and nothing moved. The false reading came from a 1055-line insertion shifting the diff block. The message stands (no history rewrite); this is the correction of record.

pending_wiring.$comment: Not done yet, on purpose: registrations.ts is being written by the #500 work and must not be touched until that has landed. This is the note of what still has to happen there.
pending_wiring.needed: a loadRerankDecisionRegistration() beside loadLongMemEvalRegistration(), plus a checkRerankDecisionRegistration() in the same shape as the other checkers, and its case in __tests__/registrations.test.ts

$comment_amendment: Version 1 of this registration carried NO RUN. At the time of this amendment — 2026-09-09T19:11Z / 21:11 CEST — no quality figure and no latency figure from the harness existed for #501; the only measurements in the plan came from the model spike (isolated model cost and example pairs, §1), not from an evaluation of the gold set or of LongMemEval. Version 1 had neither a primary endpoint nor a precedence rule between the five recommendation shapes, and it described a language guard that no code executed. Those are the reasons for this amendment. It is therefore a correction BEFORE the first number, not an adjustment to data already seen. Independently checkable evidence: (a) the model cache ~/.cache/bastra-rerank (set in rerank-model.ts, commit 57a670e) did not exist at that moment — no model had been loaded since the path was set, and without a loaded model there is no score; (b) no run artifact: --out was never passed, and the harness writes nowhere else; (c) the git history holds no result commit between cddbd70 (the harness) and this amendment.

primary_endpoint.$comment: Exactly one cell carries the recommendation. Fixed in code as PRIMARY in rerank-replay.ts so the run marks it rather than a reader inferring it from a row position.
primary_endpoint.cases: the answerable non-probe cases (584 in the full set)
primary_endpoint.estimator: paired bootstrap, 10000 resamples, percentile CI95, seed 20260909
primary_endpoint.why_this_cell: N=10 with the short passage is the only combination that can pass the latency bar at all — 26 ms p50 in the spike, while short/N=20 already sits at 52 ms against a 50 ms threshold. A lift that appears only at N=30 or on the long passage is unaffordable regardless of size, so the primary test belongs where the decision is actually made.
primary_endpoint.everything_else: EXPLORATORY. Reported with intervals, carries no recommendation — not even a weakened one. The run counts and prints how many intervals it produced (countIntervals); the review of version 1 counted 180 for the arm shape of the time, and the slices added since push it higher. At alpha=0.05 several are 'significant' under pure noise.

measurement_order.$comment: B3. Production serves slice(0, k) and the consumer drops everything below BASTRA_RECALL_FLOOR. Measuring rank on the unfiltered pool would credit the reranker for promoting a candidate the user never sees.
measurement_order.floor_free_figure: reported beside it as at_no_floor_upper_bound and named an UPPER BOUND. Never the headline.
measurement_order.open_design_question: Three consequences a shipped rerank stage would have to answer, none of them measured here, all of them for Daniel's decision. (1) BAND SEMANTICS: a stage that only REORDERS leaves the published `score` at its RRF value, so score stops being monotone in rank — and the downstream bands (30/50/100, MUST_LOAD at 100) read that score. A shipped reranker must decide what it publishes as `score`. (2) THE RESULT LIST GETS SHORTER: slice(k) runs before the floor, so a rerank that pulls sub-floor candidates forward occupies top-10 slots that the floor then removes, while the high-scoring hits that would have filled them have dropped to rank 11+. The user then sees FEWER hits than before. The harness models this correctly and the measured lift already contains it, but as a design consequence it is a product effect, not a measurement artefact, and it is at least as important for the decision as the latency. (3) isNoHome (#230, weak-result.ts:88-95) reads hits[0] and its `rrf` block, so a pure reorder changes that signal with no score question involved at all. This is why weakResult is computed on the BASELINE ranking, never on the reranked one.

degradation_gate.$comment: B2. recallHybrid fires onCandidatePool from its BM25 fallback too (search.ts:840), with raw BM25 scores in BM25 order. An ungated replay would have counted those rows inside a denominator labelled hybrid.
degradation_gate.mechanism: gatedHybridRecaller from goldset-run.ts — the same gate the gold runner uses; a degraded case stops the run
degradation_gate.telemetry: an onStage listener records vector.search wait_ms / timed_out / provider_outcome per case and the run reports dense_arm_health, so the latency protocol's discard rule is executable rather than merely stated

precedence.$comment: Evaluated in this order, FIRST MATCH WINS, default 'do not ship'.
precedence.$comment_close_is_inclusive: close_501's condition deliberately CONTAINS the negation of the three conditional shapes. Without that, putting 'close' first would make them structurally unreachable — a null primary with a large weak_result lift is exactly the case shape 3 exists for — and the ordering would be meaningless.

effect_classification.$comment: Mandatory whenever the primary comes out null. 'No effect' and 'no affordable effect' are completely different statements: the first buries the hypothesis, the second is an argument for #119.
effect_classification.no_effect: no arm at any (N, passage, model) on the gold set reaches delta >= 2.0 pp at R@3 with CI95 lower bound > 0 → close #501, the hypothesis is refuted
effect_classification.no_affordable_effect: at least one more expensive arm (N=30 and/or body, or bge) reaches that bar while the primary arm does not → close #501 for the QUERY PATH, and state explicitly that this is positive evidence for #119
effect_classification.$comment_consistency: The exploratory arms still carry no recommendation, but they do carry this one classification — consistent, because the classification recommends shipping nothing.

language_guard.$comment: B1. Version 1 claimed in prose that ms-marco 'may not be scored' on the German set while ModelSpec.languages was read by no code: --models ms-marco --gold <german> ran over 272 German cases. The guard was the human typing the flag.
language_guard.mechanism: assertLanguagesAllowed(spec, langs) in rerank-model.ts, called by the runner before any model loads; refuses de/en outside the model's measured set
language_guard.not_checked: neutral and mixed — they belong to no language pool, and refusing them would rule out 205 of 584 cases for every model
language_guard.test: the test asserts the REFUSAL, and was verified to go red when the guard is neutered
language_guard.scope_limit: The guard checks the QUERY language, not the passage language. Passages come from the vault and are German regardless of what language the query is in, so the guard only holds while vault language and query language coincide. That is true for both registered sets — on gold only bilingual models are registered, and on LongMemEval corpus and questions are both English — but it is a property of the data, not of the guard, and is recorded here so a future set with a language split between corpus and queries is not silently admitted.

outcome.$comment: Filled in AFTER the run. The bars above are unchanged from version 2, which was fixed before any number existed — compare them against this block to check that the recommendation was not fitted to the result.
outcome.why_no_effect_and_not_unaffordable: The best exploratory arm anywhere is bge/short N=10 at +2.2 pp with CI [-1.0, +5.5]. It clears the 2.0 pp POINT threshold and fails ONLY on the interval, which contains 0 — the registered bar requires both (delta >= 2.0 pp AND CI95 lower bound > 0). The classification therefore stands, but the margin is smaller than an earlier wording claimed: that wording cited +1.9 pp from a discarded preliminary run and said the value was below the point threshold. It was not, and the error ran in our own favour. What does hold: no arm produces a lift whose interval excludes 0, so there is none that latency could have been too expensive for.
outcome.robustness: Null on three independent cuts: full denominator +0.2, reachable subset (n=342) +0.3 [-5.3, +5.8], descriptive axis (n=447) +0.0 [-4.3, +4.3]. The dilution hypothesis does not carry.
outcome.control_set: LongMemEval, 500 questions, 3 models: ALL 18 rows negative with every CI entirely below zero, main arm -9.4 pp [-12.6, -6.4]. Protocol baseline recall_any@20 = 99.6 %, matching #500's published figure. The control SUPPORTS the recommendation; it does not create it — the gold set decides and would have decided the same alone.
outcome.bilingual_surcharge: Answered: none. ms-marco (English-only) gives no advantage over the bilingual en-de on the English set — identical at body/N=10 (-5.8) and worse at short (-10.0 vs -9.4).
outcome.latency_step_not_run: #501 step 2 is conditional on a real lift ('only if the lift is real'). There is none, so no latency run was performed.

shapes_not_evaluable.only_on_weak_result: isWeakResult fired on 0 of 584 gold cases and 0 of 500 LongMemEval questions — the shape was not merely empty but unmeasurable.
shapes_not_evaluable.above_pool_size: Gold set: the pool is a constant 40 deep by construction, so the median split leaves one bucket empty. LongMemEval: measurable (248/252) and harmful in both halves.

outcome.bars_not_relaxed: No bar was lowered and no threshold moved: decision_bars, primary_endpoint, slices and guards are byte-identical to the version fixed before any number existed. The primary was not moved to the reachable subset although its dilution (19.9 % structural non-contributors) was quantified and known — it would have read +0.3 instead of +0.2. Honest qualification: the by_kind split WAS added to the harness after the coverage numbers were known and because of them. It was deliberately NOT added to `slices` in this registration, precisely because its favourable direction was already known — see the measurement plan §8.9. It is reported as exploratory and carries no recommendation.
outcome.floor_effect: Measured, and it corrects a claim an earlier report made twice, in both directions. The score floor changes the served figures in 17 of 36 cells — 0 at N=10 (which includes the primary cell), 6 at N=20, 11 at N=30. In 15 of the 17 it RAISES the served hit rate, because `served` cuts to k and then filters, so dropping a sub-floor entry moves a deeper candidate up an index position. Two separate conclusions follow and only one is evidence: the PRECONDITION of the open design question is demonstrated (a reranker does pull sub-floor candidates into the served ranks at N >= 20), while the feared HARM is not — what remains after filtering is fewer entries, not worse ones. How much shorter the list becomes is explicitly NOT measured: the artifacts carry hit rates, not list lengths. Whether a shorter list is itself a product disadvantage is a product question, not a measurement question, and stays open.

run_out.$comment: Where the raw artifacts live. An earlier state of this registration named none, and the report cited a session scratchpad path with mode 0600 — so an independent reviewer could not check a single figure. The evidence excerpt beside this file (rerank-results.json) carries a sha256 per artifact plus the numbers the decision rests on, so the decision is checkable even without the large files.
run_out.$comment_rerun: A re-run does NOT restore this evidence. The gold pass measured a live vault: two runs over the same set differed by one case at depth 30 because two memories were written between them (1171 -> 1173 vectors). Worse, that run predates the vault fingerprint (d383f22), so the exact vault it saw cannot be reconstructed at all. Runs from d383f22 onward carry the fingerprint; this one does not, and the excerpt says so.
